text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: High p99 latency on /v1/generate (dedicated pool: dp-east-4). Severity: P1 -> paging oncall.

Metrics snapshot (rolling 5m): p50=120ms, p95=780ms, p99=2.1s, streaming-stalls=4.2% (was 0.3%). Queue depth for dp-east-4: avg=220 (normal 40). Autoscaler handshake failures: 23/5m.

Amber (oncall): Ack. Oncall taking. Paging Ben and Carla for infra/sre. @Ben @Carla please. Any immediate mitigation suggestions?

Ben (sre): I'm looking. Can someone paste the autoscaler/controller logs? I see repeated handshake timeouts to pool leader: 

```
2026-03-15T03:06:41Z controller: handshake to dp-east-4 leader failed: timeout after 10s
2026-03-15T03:06:42Z controller: enqueue warmup job -> pending (warmup-queue-length=198)
2026-03-15T03:07:10Z controller: heartbeat mismatch: expected seq 482, got 0
2026-03-15T03:07:12Z autoscaler: unable to attach instance: dial tcp timeout
```

Carla (infra): Correlating with node telemetry now. dp-east-4 leader host (ip: 10.12.98.21) had repeated kubelet restarts around 03:05Z. Warmup pods are stuck in Init: 

```
$ kubectl get pods -n dedicated-dp-east-4 | egrep "warmup|leader"
warmup-0-abcde   0/1 Init:ImagePullBackOff  20m
leader-10-12-98-21 CrashLoopBackOff  12m
```

Carla: Looking at system logs on the leader node: kernel OOM killer evicted the heartbeat-agent binary process, then kubelet restarted and the leader lost its active state. Image pull failures for warmup come from a transient registry auth error (403) at same timeframe.

Devon (runtime): Streaming stalls line up with KV cache coldpath amplification after leader flapped. When leader disappears, many active streams rehydrate KV and cause simultaneous long tail token generation. We're seeing stall patterns: token generation p99 ~6s during coldpath spikes. Two mitigations: force warmup/coldpath prefill, and reduce concurrency for non-critical customers to lower instantaneous load.

Amber (oncall): Mitigation plan (short list):
1) Emergency scale: add +2 GPU nodes to dp-east-4 (override autoscaler) to absorb backlog.
2) Force warmup jobs to run immediately on new nodes (kickstart prefill).
3) Route non-critical/low-tier traffic to fallback pool (dp-east-standby) for next 10m.
4) Apply throttle to top noisy customers by route to shed excess qps.
5) Notify support and product for possible customer impact.

Carla: I can run the emergency scale and patch registry creds for warmup image. Command I will run: 

```
# emergency override - adds 2 GPUs to pool
redwoodctl pool scale --pool dp-east-4 --add 2 --force

# kickstart warmup tasks
redwoodctl pool warmup --pool dp-east-4 --mode force --concurrency 8
```

Ben: I'll open a quick routing rule to divert non-critical traffic (routes tagged "best-effort") to dp-east-standby. Command: 

```
redwoodctl route update --selector tier=best-effort --target dp-east-standby --ttl 600
```

Ben: Executed scale override at 03:09Z. New instances provisioning. Provision logs: 

```
03:09:10Z scheduler: allocating 2 gpus -> instance id i-0a12cd34
03:09:45Z instance i-0a12cd34: attaching to cluster
03:10:30Z instance i-0a12cd34: agent connected, warming
03:10:55Z warmup job started on i-0a12cd34
```

Devon: Kicked off forced warmup. Running a shallow prefill for top 500 prefixes to rebuild KV caches. Warmup estimated ~60-120s to meaningfully reduce coldpath pressure.

Erin (support): Drafting customer notices. Which tenants are likely impacted? We have short tail spikes across many routes, but high-volume customers Xcorp and Ystream show increased error budgets. I'll prepare a targeted message: "We observed elevated request latency for generation endpoints between 03:05Z-03:20Z. We're applying routing mitigations now; we'll update when stable."

Amber: Status check at 03:12Z?

Ben: New instances are connected. Controller handshake retried and succeeded at 03:11:58Z. Autoscaler handshake errors reduced. Current queue depth: 212 -> 140. p95/p99 trending down.

Carla: Registry creds patched at 03:13Z, warmup pods that were ImagePullBackOff started pulling and now initializing. leader node rejoined after kubelet clean restart; heartbeat agent restarted and re-registered.

Devon: After warmup run (03:15Z) we see KV cache hit rate jump from 28% -> 79% for active prefixes. Streaming stalls dropped from 4.2% -> 0.6%. p99 fell from 2.1s -> 610ms. p95 ~ 320ms.

Amber: Good. Implemented traffic diversion for best-effort routes; Ben confirmed route change. Are we seeing any 5xx spike?

Ben: 5xx briefly spiked to 1.8% at the peak (03:07Z-03:11Z) mostly 502 from the warmup backlog. Now down to 0.15%.

Erin: Support message sent to affected customers (Xcorp, Ystream) with the mitigation summary and ETA for postmortem.

Frank (product): Thanks team. Can we confirm customer-visible SLA hits? Frank: looks like Xcorp lost ~0.6% of successful request rate during window; we'll consolidate with account team.

Amber: Current action items (post-incident):
- (Carla) Investigate root cause: why heartbeat-agent was OOM'd and why leader node experienced kubelet flaps. Check kernel OOM logs + recent memory pressure events.
- (Ben) Add guardrail to avoid autoscaler handshake thrashing: longer backoff on handshake retries and better metrics to detect leader flapping earlier.
- (Devon) Add an on-pool coldpath prefill policy when a leader reboots (auto-trigger warmup).
- (Ben/Carla) Add registry credential monitoring/alerting to catch transient 403s earlier.
- (Amber) Run a small follow-up test: simulate leader restart in staging and measure warmup cadence and handoff behavior.

Carla: Early hypothesis: node-level memory pressure (OOM) + transient registry auth fail caused a double-hit: leader flapped, warmup couldn't populate, controller kept scaling but handshakes failed until new agents re-registered.

Ben: I'll file INC-1729994 (root-cause investigation) and include logs + timeline.

Amber: Closing the page after stabilization. Final metrics (03:05Z -> 03:25Z window): p95 peak 780ms -> baseline 320ms; p99 peak 2.1s -> 610ms; streaming-stalls peak 4.2% -> 0.6%. Queue depth normalized to 38.

Erin: Noted for postmortem and customer comms. Anything else?

Devon: Recommend adding a short-circuit so when leader disconnects, we immediately trigger a low-noise prefill for the top N prefixes instead of full-throttle rehydration. I'll draft a proposal.

Amber: Thanks all. I'll keep INC-1729994 as the follow-up. If anyone sees regression, re-page. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> severity downgraded to P3. Incident channel will remain open for 24h for follow-ups.
